model.title: Vance's reported doubts modestly shift GOP nomination odds
model.summary: The forecast slightly lowers JD Vance’s Republican nomination odds and reallocates that probability to Marco Rubio and Ron DeSantis, reflecting reports that Vance is uncertain about running despite continuing to lead recent primary polling. No new general-election polls or sustained changes in the broader national evidence support changes to the election outlook or uncertainty.

overview.summary:
Democrats are favored to win the 2028 presidential election in this forecast, which projects 300 electoral votes for the party within a plausible range of 220 to 380 and a national popular vote margin of about 4.5 points. The forecast's closest states are Arizona, North Carolina, Nevada, Georgia and Pennsylvania, where margins are narrow enough that the outcome there could change with modest shifts.

The lean rests mainly on the national environment. Democrats won the 2026 national House vote by about 13 points and hold 250 seats with 28 still counting, while President Trump's net approval stands near -25. Unemployment was 4.1 percent in October. National polling averages show no measurable lead for either party this far from the election, so the forecast relies more on fundamentals than on current head-to-head polls.
overview.watch: Newsom's expected decision on a 2028 run in early January, along with the next economic reports, could shift the Democratic nomination picture and the national environment.

nominations.D: Kamala Harris is the most likely Democratic nominee in the forecast, but the field remains open, with Gavin Newsom, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Pete Buttigieg, Jon Ossoff and Josh Shapiro all with meaningful chances, and Ossoff at 15 percent in the latest primary poll.
nominations.R: JD Vance leads the Republican nomination field in the forecast and in most polling, followed by Marco Rubio, who posted 33 percent in the latest poll, and Ron DeSantis, who posted 14 percent, though Vance's willingness to run after the midterms remains uncertain.

storylines.title: Democrats post a sweeping 2026 midterm result
storylines.detail: Democrats won the national House vote by 13.17 points and made broad statewide gains, including victories in Texas and Georgia. Florida remained a Republican outlier relative to the national House result, and the forecast retains its national shift and limited Florida-specific adjustment.

storylines.title: The fundamentals point in different directions
storylines.detail: Presidential net approval is -24.6, slightly lower than the -23.7 reading on November 1, while the latest available economy assessment continues to favor Democrats overall. October inflation rose 0.4%, but the economic index remains unavailable, so the forecast does not treat that report alone as a sustained change.

storylines.title: The Democratic primary remains wide open
storylines.detail: Harris remains near the top of the polling picture, while the November 11 poll placed Ossoff at 15%, Newsom at 13%, and Ocasio-Cortez at 12%. Newsom expects to decide on a run in early January, Booker is organizing in South Carolina, and the recommended calendar change for New Mexico has not settled the field.

storylines.title: Shapiro's reelection and groundwork strengthen his case
storylines.detail: Shapiro's reelection, large margin, federal PAC, and reporting about his post-election groundwork keep him in the 2028 conversation. The forecast retains the nomination chance already assigned to him.

storylines.title: Ossoff's reelection fuels renewed speculation
storylines.detail: Ossoff's Georgia victory continues to fuel speculation, and the latest primary poll gave him 15%, above his prior polling average. His earlier statement that he would not run continues to temper the forecast's estimate.

storylines.title: Vance leads GOP polling as Rubio and DeSantis draw attention
storylines.detail: Vance remains the Republican primary polling leader, though recent reports continue to describe uncertainty about whether he will run after the midterm losses. storylines.title: AOC's team activity adds to signs of 2028 preparation
storylines.detail: A progressive group has launched an effort to draft Ocasio-Cortez, and recent reporting describes a team shake-up as she weighs a 2028 decision. These signals stop short of a declared campaign, so the forecast retains her current nomination chance.

storylines.title: Booker begins early organizing in South Carolina
storylines.detail: Booker is scheduled to visit South Carolina twice this month, with reporting describing the visits as the official start to his 2028 effort. The forecast already modestly raised his nomination odds, while the field remains unsettled this far from the primaries.

revisions.title: Latest primary poll modestly lifts Ossoff, Rubio and DeSantis
revisions.summary: The model modestly raises Jon Ossoff’s Democratic nomination odds after the latest poll placed him above his polling average, and makes smaller increases for Marco Rubio and Ron DeSantis after strong showings in the same poll. No new general-election polls or sustained change in the broader national evidence supports adjustments to the general-election outlook.

revisions.title: Small primary-odds shifts follow new polling and candidate signals
revisions.summary: The model modestly raises Jon Ossoff’s Democratic nomination odds after a recent poll put him above his prior polling average. It also makes small increases for Marco Rubio and Ron DeSantis, while leaving the national outlook, state adjustments and uncertainty unchanged because no new general-election polls or sustained shift in the broader evidence is reported.

revisions.title: Recent primary polling modestly reshapes nomination odds
revisions.summary: The forecast makes small changes to both nomination contests, reflecting recent primary polling: Ossoff gains slightly among Democrats, while Rubio and DeSantis gain among Republicans. No new general-election polls or sustained change in the national outlook supports broader adjustments.

revisions.title: Newsom's January decision modestly lifts his nomination odds
revisions.summary: The model slightly raises Gavin Newsom’s Democratic nomination chance after he said he expects to decide on a presidential run in early January, shifting the added probability from Other. No new general-election polls or sustained change in the national outlook supports broader adjustments.

revisions.title: Booker gains modestly after starting early 2028 organizing
revisions.summary: The model slightly raises Cory Booker's Democratic nomination odds after reports that he is visiting South Carolina as he begins organizing for 2028, shifting the added probability from Other. No new general-election polls or sustained change in the national outlook supports broader adjustments.
